agencies.
8.    Capacity utilization of captive Power Plant
The Committee  was informed that  the captive  power plant is capable  of supplying power  to the Smelter. However,
the power system is connected to Orissa grid, which is unreliable and unstable.   The voltage and frequency variations
are high and at times the  system trips   due to external   fault, causing a total black out of the grid This was  a  frequent
phenomenon earlier .  The situation   at present is  better after NTPC super thermal power plant  came into existence.
The Committee was further  informed that    frequent   power interruption  has detrimental effect on pot operation.  In
1998, the pot  line,  handling of metal at cast house, power failures and excessive heat in summer  were some  of the
major factors  which led to deterioration of  some essential parameters of  pot line and finally some pots were  stopped
to survive. However after  de-bottlenecking of carbon plant, the inputs like  anode and bath are matching to pot line
requirement.  Similarly, addition of billet  casting facility and Strip  Casting plant are  helping to evacuate the hot metal. 
With the improved grid position, it is expected to operate the plant in future without much problem.   With the 
expansion of Smelter  the   capacity  of power plant is also being enhanced from 720MW to 960MW.
The Committee was  informed that the  de-bottlenecking of Smelter was carried  out at a cost of Rs.49.12 crore.  This 
was mainly  in the Carbon area of Smelter Plant, which was proving  to be  a bottleneck for the   Smelter plant to attain
its designed capacity.  The de-bottlenecking of Smelter has helped in attaining 480 pot operation (100% capacity
utilisation)  in  Smelter.  No further de-bottlenecking is  planned in Smelter.  However,   for the third pot line under
Smelter expansion, the above aspect has been taken care of. During the course of oral evidence on 10
th April, 2001, the
CMD informed that Nalco is running at over 100% capacity.
The Committee noted that inadequate checks and maintenance caused the shunting of pots in the smelter in April and
June 1998 resulting in less then 100% utilization.
The Committee recommends that adequate safeguards be built within the system to avoid such recurrence in future.

13. Research and Development
Nalco has two independent R&D centers at both M&R Complex, Damonjodi as well as in S&P Complex at Angul. Both
the centers have been recognized by Ministry of Science & Technology, Govt. of India. Both the centers are equipped
with facilities to take care of plant related process, problems and product development activities for value addition. It
also continues to carry out small experiments to improve the quality of inputs in production process, to improve
productivity and quality of product. The R&D center has successfully implemented projects like Special grade Alumina
pilot and commercial plant and Zeolite "A" commercial plant. Further value-added products from waste materials like
fly ash and red mud have been developed. Some process technologies have been patented. Nalco has taken up some
collaborative R&D project with CSIR laboratory, IIT etc. in areas of process and product development. Nalco's R&D
scientists have received national and international awards like NRDC Award, WIPO Gold Medal, ICI Award etc.
The Committee appreciated several of the value added products made from fly ash. The Committee also noted that the
captive power plant of Nalco generates a considerable amount of fly ash which can be used to make value added
products. During the course of oral evidence on Demands for Grants  the CMD stated  "As far as research and
development wing is concerned, we have developed a special grade alumina and Zeolite.  The special grade alumina
project will be completed in December, 2001. Then we have also undertaken research project in collaboration with
Russia. This research project will help converting iron in the red mud to pig iron".
The Committee recommends that Nalco should explore means of using its R&D output for finding viable means to
commercially dispose of the fly ash. Besides the Committee also feels that  R&D effort should be channelised to explore
ways to improve the quality of alumina and other secondary aluminium products. Efforts may be made to complete the
special grade project as per schedule. The Committee also hopes that the research project in collaboration with Russia to
convert iron from red mud to pig iron would be completed early and would be successful.

15.       Breach of  NALCO’s  fly ash pond at Angul.
The Committee visited  Angul captive power plant on 23
rd January, 2001.  The Committee also visited the fly ash pond
of Nalco and the place where the breach took place. The Committee enquired into the reasons for the breach of the fly
ash pond which took place on 31.12.2000 as a result of which heavy ash with water drained from the pond and a fly ash
flood took place. This had a severe impact on the soil fertility of over twenty-three villages. Acute drinking water
problem arose from  this and around one thousand acres of land got adversely affected. The Committee was informed
that an inquiry Committee had been constituted to inquire into the reasons for the mishap.  During the course of oral
evidence on Demands for Grants of Ministry of Mines the CMD of NALCO  informed that the breach has been
repaired. Regarding compensation the CMD stated: "The district administration headed by the Collector, in consultation
with various MLAs and some important people in the Angul area, has worked out the compensation. We have entirely
accepted the compensation package worked out by the Collector. Out of about 1100 people who have been affected, a
list of about 740 people has been released. We have already paid the compensation to those people for the damaged
crops as well as for the ash that has been deposited on their particular land. The Collector was of the view that 100%
compensation should not be made in the first instance. He says that let them remove the ash that is collected on their
lands first. After they remove that, then we can pay the balance 40%. In addition to that, as a gesture, we have provided
them with piped water supply, costing us about Rs.5.7 crores. It has nothing to do with the breach or the compensation.
We have already paid Rs.1 crore to the Collector. So, whatever compensation was recommended by the District
Administration has been paid by us."
The Committee recommends that adequate safeguards be built within the system to prevent  recurrence of such incidents
in future. The Committee also recommends that stringent  action be taken against the officials  responsible for the
breach of fly ash pond. The Committee would also like to know the recommendations and action taken on the enquiry

18.   Peripheral area development
The Committee was informed that Nalco plays a catalytic role for improving the infrastructure and general quality of
life of the people living in the periphery of the Company’s plants and facilities through implementation of a systematic
programme of periphery development with particular emphasis on rehabilitation of displaced families and weaker
sections of the society. The Committee was further informed that in both Angul and Damanjodi units of Nalco,
periphery development activities are planned by the Company’s peripheral development  Committees in consultation
with local govt authorities.  These  Committees formulate the annual plans and estimate taking into account the needs of
the Peripheral Villages alongwith the views of State  Agencies and  elected representatives of the  localities.  Works are
mostly  executed  through the placement of funds with the local Government  authorities.  However, depending upon 
the nature of the work some of the jobs are directly executed by the Company.  The Company officials monitor the jobs
for which  funds are  sanctioned and obtain execution/completion certificate from the  concerned agencies from time to
time.
The Committee however was not satisfied with the progress made under the peripheral area development programme.
The Committee considers the peripheral area as an integral part of  Nalco and its development would generate
tremendous goodwill for NALCO.  The CMD of NALCO  stated "Every year, we spend about one crore on the
peripheral development of the two projects i.e. Angul and Damanjodi." The CMD also informed "We have allocated 0.5
per cent of the profit for peripheral development. Now we have definitely planned to increase this. Our profits have
increased substantially. We also want to increase the outlay for peripheral development. I am happy to inform you that
the Ministry of Mines has recently taken a very important decision that it advised us to include the local MPs in the
Committees we have set up for peripheral development". "In case of Angul and Koraput, we will include the Members
of Parliament from these particular regions so that they will get an idea as to what the peripheral development would
be."  As regards ex-servicemen and women, the Secretary Ministry of Mines stated  "As far as ex-servicemen are
concerned, we have not taken up anything. I totally agree with you. In fact, there are two shortcomings. One is regarding
the ex-servicemen and the other is regarding women strength. It is also quite low. These are two important
shortcomings. We will take up these two things and do something."
The Committee recommends that greater stress should be placed upon proper monitoring of the peripheral area
development programmes. The Committee strongly recommends that higher allocation be made for peripheral area
development. Besides the Committee was distressed to note that despite Angul area having a large number of ex-
servicemen,   adequate representation in terms of employment in Nalco has not been given to them. The Committee
hopes that adequate representative be given to Ex-servicemen.
19.       Some problems
The Committee   has been given to understand that  NALCO is facing some problems and         their  solution  is 
required  for increasing Nalco's  market  share and  sales revenue. The     problems are :-
Since lot of scrap aluminium of inferior quality is  being imported into the country and is being used by the aluminium
down stream industries, Nalco as a quality conscious primary producer is facing problems in competing with such
upgraded and low quality scrap metal.
The Committee recommends that  the Government may kindly consider enhancing the import duty on such scraps to the
same level as that of primary aluminium metal.
Due to non-uniform Sales Tax Policy still prevailing in certain states, the company is
facing problems in competing with metal  sold/traded  from  these  areas. This  not  only causes loss to the Government
exchequer, due to less tax  realization   but   also  creates unhealthy competition between different
marketing/distribution channels. It was requested that at least for primary aluminium metal, for which there are limited
number  of producers, uniform Sales Tax structure is followed.

The plant for production of Zeolite-A, used in detergent manufacture is in advanced stage of commissioning. Zeolite-A
has been scientifically proven and commercially implemented as eco-friendly material for this application. However,
most of the detergent  manufacturers are still using STPP (sodium tri poly-phosphate), which is a pollutant and,
therefore, has been banned in, many western countries. When STPP mixes in the water system, it helps in growth of
algae, which extracts dissolved oxygen from water, thereby, the aquatic life perishes.
The Committee takes a serious view of this and recommends  that keeping in view our concern for         environmental
protection, use of STPP may be banned by the Government through an appropriate legislation. Besides, incentives may
kindly be given for use of Zeolite by exempting Excise Duty on this product for a period of at least 5 years.
It was requested that Railways should   accord priority for movement of Nalco's traffic and make available adequate
number of locos to achieve turnaround of Nalco Wagons as planned by RITES.
The Committee recommends that Ministry of Mines may take up the matter with Railways.

RECOMMENDATION  No.3
 
1.         Joint Mechanism for appraising term loans and working capital
 
The Committee came to know that there is no single agency for lending the term loan and working capital to SSI units’
requirement exceeding Rs. 10 lakh which leaves the SSI entrepreneurs to run from pillar to post.  Under the circumstances, the

54th Report

Committee feels that situation may improve a lot if there is a mechanism for joint appraisal of term lending and working
capital loan for higher amount (about Rs. 10 lakh) so that there is no gap in the sanction of two types of loans.  The measures,
if undertaken, not only will save the time but also the money for SSI entrepreneurs, the Committee feels.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
With  the enhancement of loan limit under Composite Loan Scheme from Rs.10 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs, most of the tiny
units would be covered and the problem of approaching separate institutions for meeting different requirements would be
resolved.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION  No.8
           
2.
         Prime Minister’s announcement of package for SSI sector.
 
(i)                   Presently, the Government has given the capital subsidy in select sectors (under Credit Linked Capital Subsidy
Scheme). The Committee feels that Ministry  of  SSI  & ARI   should  examine  whether  such  capital  subsidy  is 
required in other sectors of SSI for technology upgradation, if so, the Ministry should take up the issue at
appropriate level.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
There is scope for inclusion of more sectors in the scheme.  While formulating the scheme, it has  to be acknowledged that
the identification of technology is a continuous process.  The Scheme envisages that a Technical  Advisory Committee would
be set up under the Chairmanship of Secretary (SSI&ARI) to identify the state-of–the-art technology and benchmark existing
and new technologies.
 
(ii)                 The Committee further observes that since sickness of SSI units  is a chronic problem, a serious thought and
timely action is required for rehabilitation of currently sick but potentially viable SSI units.  The Committee hopes
that RBI will be successful.  In its current efforts to draw a detailed, transparent and non-discretionary guidelines
and same will be issued for effective implementation before the sick but potentially viable SSI units  go beyond the
point of no-return.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
RBI has recently constituted a Committee under the Chairmanship of  Shri S.S. Kohli, Chairman, IBA to draw revised
detailed, transparent and non-   discretionary guidelines for rehabilitation of current sick and potentially viable     SSI units.
 
(iii)                The Committee feels that  policy/package which has been envisaged/ extending to SSI will not suffer the problem
of  the implementation of gap.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
Action on most of the  measures announced in the policy package has been initiated/completed.
 
(iv)               The Committee recommends that Ministry of SSI & ARI while furnishing ATN on the recommendations
contained in the present Report will give detailed note with regard to action taken and its impact on each and every
scheme under the present package for SSI units.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
The action on various points of the comprehensive policy package has been  taken  indicated against each in the
Annexure.  The reaction/impact of certain measures  like doubling excise duty exemption limit, enhancing the coverage of
loans under Credit Guarantee Scheme, raising the project cost limit under NEF, launching of  Credit Linked Capital Subsidy
Scheme for Technology Upgradation, has been positive and overwhelming as many prominent SSI Associations have lauded
the Government efforts to strengthen the SSI sector and enhance its competitiveness both domestically and globally. 
However, with regard to other measures,  it is too early to assess the impact.
 
In regard to point   No.15 in the Annexure submitted by the Ministry on the Recommendation No.8, the Committee felt

RECOMMENDATION NO.1 
 
5.         Meeting of Working Capital Requirement
 
The Committee recommends that steps should be taken to ensure credit facilitation to SSI units upto 20% of SSI
production/turnover.
 
5.1       Comments/Action Taken
 
RBI has advised the banks for enhancement in limit from Rs.4 crores to Rs.5 crores for computation of aggregate
working capital requirements of SSI units on the basis of minimum  20% of their projected annual turnover vide circular
No.PLNFS No.BC7.3/06.02.31/98-99 dated 1.3.1999.Following the discussions at the meeting of Group of Ministers on SSI,
RBI has   reiterated the  instructions contained in its circular dated the 1
st March,1999 to commercial banks for providing
working capital based on this specified norm  vide circular No. RPCD PLNFS. BC.16/06.02.31/2000-01 dated 15 th
Sept.,2000.
 
5.2              Further Observations/ Recommendations
 
            During the course of interaction with the representatives of the Banks in Mumbai on  the Committee was informed by
the representatives of the banks that the assessment of the limit, it is somewhat cumbersome procedure but in case of SSI it has
been agreed that 20% of the turnover should be given as a limit and it enables them to look after about 5 cycles in a year. Now
this 20% is of projected sales. It has ben  seen often there are differences of views between borrower and the banker about
the    projections  given  that  creates many difficulties. Apart from that, the procedure is very simple and normally the bank
should not deduct or deduce once they arrive at the 20% of the sales figure. Generally 20%  in all SSI it is a very clear
situation in the bank branches that they have to abide by the Naik Committee norms which is 20% of the projected turnover. 
Now the projected turnover, sometimes people in their anxiety to get a slightly better proportion of the bank finance put it
unrealistically.
 
5.3       The Committee feels  that proper evaluation of the past trends should be taken into account together with the capacity
of the unit  to increase the turnover depending on availabilities of orders and infrastructure to extend the work orders   by the
Banks so as to arrive at a realistic figure regarding the turnover. The Committee recommends that the Branch Managers
should work out a realistic target so that the 20% is met under all circumstances. The Committee also feels that the Branch
Managers who meet their targets should be suitably rewarded.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO.2
 
6.         Sustainable rate of interest:
The Committee not only hopes that the commercial banks will lend  credit to SSI units at sustainable rate of interest
but expects strongly that Government will chalk out adequate incentive to induce commercial banks for extending loan at
sustainable rate of interest.
 
6.1       Comments/Action Taken
 
The Banks endeavour is to charge the most competitive interest rates on advances to SSI units.  Recently, RBI has cut
down the rate of interest by 1% in two phases.  It is expected that the bank will pass it to their  borrowers.  The recent lowering
down  of bank rate will help to reduce the cost of credit  further.
 
6.2       Further Observations/ Recommendations
 
During the course of interaction with representatives of financial institutions and banks the representative from
Maharashtra State Finance Corporation  stated that the health of SFCs is linked to the health of SSIs, When the SSIs do not do
well, the SFCs don't do well. One of the things that the SFC founds itself as the MSFC because of the narrowing gap between
the borrowing cost and the lending rate of interest that is inter spread. The overall cost of borrowing ranges between 8-10%
while the overall cost of borrowing is 13.50%. The main source of raising funds is the re-finance from SIDBI and IDBI which
charge something like 11.5% and 12.5% respectively. The State Government charges a guarantee fee of 2% so that raising the
cost of borrowing is 13.5%. The interest spread therefore that is available even if they  take only 1.5%, they  can only lend at
15%. In a regime of falling interest rates in the market if  they lend at 15%, and that is the least rate they can lend at, what

54th Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/54threport.htm[04-07-2016 12:13:29]
really happens is that good borrowers repay faster and the other problem is that SIDBI and IDBI do not retire high cost funds.
 
6.3       The Committee has noted with concern the narrowing gap between the cost of borrowing and the cost of lending for
financial institutions. The Committee recommends  the possibility  should be explored by SIDBI and IDBI to retire the old
high cost dues so as to facilitate the fresh loan process and give impetus to SSIs. The Committee also recommends that steps
to  evolve necessary mechanism so that the financial health of SFCs is restored.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 4
 
7.           Wider  Access to Bank Finance
 
The Committee strongly feels that the Govt. should undertake following measures for enabling SSI units to have access to
bank finance-
 
 (i)        Undertaking of orientation course and adequate training for staff/officers of commercial banks for a change in the
attitude for lending to SSI sector.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
(i)             As per the periodical reports received from RBI, regular  training programmes are  organised  by  the Banks for 
staff/officers so as to improve their work performance besides sensitising them towards better service delivery to
SSI sector.
 
Further  Observations/Recommendations
 
The Committee has observed that a change in the mental attitude of the bank officials at the lower levels is required. The
Bank officials should take a proactive role in encouraging entrepreneurship and provide both technological advise and
financial inputs to make the SSI sector strong.
 
 
(ii)                 Simplification of procedures for obtaining credit from Banks.  Arrangement may be made for land mortgage
instead of stamp duty for enabling SSI units to obtain credit from bank against land mortgage.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
As per the periodical  reports received from RBI banks, there is   continuous endeavour to simplify their procedures
with a view to prompt and efficient service to the SSI units.
 
Further  Observations/Recommendations
 
The Committee has noted that an entrepreneur has still to run from pillar to post and completing all procedural
formalities is still a nightmare. The Committee recommends that further simplification of the procedure may be done on an
urgent and priority basis.
 
(iii)                Govt. should create conducive climate for development of factoring services through appropriate policy
prescription/ legislative changes to ease problems relating to stamp duty, registration fee, assignment of Debt
etc.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
The Ministry of SSI & ARI has constituted a Committee on factoring services  under the Chairmanship of Joint
Secretary.  The Committee has prepared a draft legislation on factoring services which is under consideration of the GOI
 
Further  Observations/Recommendations
 
The Committee would like to know the latest status of the above draft legislation including the steps taken by the
Ministry to expedite the consideration and approval of the legislation.

(iv)               Recapitalisation  and revamping of SFCs with the help of SIDBI and IDBI enabling SFCs to lend fixed capital
to SSI units.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
A Committee on restructuring SFCs headed  by  the Chairman, IDBI, has submitted its Report to the Government of
India.
 
Further  Observations/Recommendations
 
The Committee would like to know the latest status of the report including the follow up action if any taken by the

Popularisation of Venture Capital Fund
 
The committee feels that the Commercial banks should come forward in launching venture capital funds in all its

9.

9.1       Although SIDBI has come forward with Technology Development and Modernisation Fund (TDMF) Scheme in order
to assist SSIs at its prime lending rates but the Committee,  taking   into   account   the   magnitude   of  the problem of
technological  obsolescence in SSI sector, feels that Govt. should come forward to set up Technology Upgradation and

9.2       Comments/Action Taken

institutions. The Committee recommends that steps to build up a strong culture of venture capital for SSIs is required to be
built up.

enable them to face global competition. The ministry can make a think tank with adequate support so that flow of latest

make a real difference at the grass root level are to be given special recognistion in the form of annual certificate award etc.
and  the Committee also recommends that cases of banks who have been particularly successful need to be emulated and
followed up by other banks.

Sector may be submitted to the Committee.

that KVIC continues to have huge inventories and it reflects on the lack of marketing expertise within KVIC. The Committee
also feels that KVIC has not been able to change according to the market demand and has not been able to develop a suitable a
marketing strategy. The Committee recommends that immediate steps to evolve a effective strategy be taken in this regard.
(Para No.12.2 )

GENERAL RECOMMENDATION

RECOMMENDATION 
Steps to Increase Demand 
Government may take following steps in order to increase the consumption of steel which 
will automatically increase the demands of steel in various sectors of economy:-
(i) Envisaging Mega- infrastructural projects like roatl. Power ports, dams, water 
pipelines, Airports etc and speedy implementation of these projects say in 3 to 5 
years; 
(ii) Reduction in safe life of LPG cylinders from existing 20 years to 15 years; 
(iii) Promotion of made in India Steel for infrastructure projects, especially those 
projects which are financed 100% by Indian Companies . Made in India steel 
must be used for construction of bridges and roads. 
(iv) .Encouraging the use of steel wheelbarrows instead of allowing to carry material 
on head; 
(v) Replacement of the use of bamboo scaffolding by steel pipe structure; 
(vi) Banning usage of health hazardous asbestos corrugated sheet both for domestic 
and industrial cladding purpose; 
(vii) Promotion of steel usage in making of truck body; and 
(viii) Encouraging usage of steel houses in earthquake prone zone. 
The measures above will result into multifold growth in areas like housing construction 
etc. And ultimately gross domestic product with go up, besides improving the health of India 
Steel Industry.

INTEGRATED NATIONAL STEEL POLICY 
5. 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee reiterates the recommendation made in 30th Report ( of Department 
Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry) to have an "Integrated National Steel 
Policy" comprising of all the segments of the Steel Industry and a policy statement which can 
land the Steel Industry to a place where it can open the account in the new millennium with 
cherished vision and rosy hopes and aspirations. Such National Steel Policy, embedded within 
overall national ,policy and priority, should be formulated while keeping in mind the SWOT 
analysis (strength, weaknesses, opportunitie s and threats) of Indian Steel Industry vis-a-vis world 

Steel Industry.. National Steel Policy should incorporate mutual coherence and cp-existence of 
Public and Private sector and reveal the policy with regard to investment-decision, humM 
resource management, pricing-policy in a liberalized and globalised economy, export import 
policy, structural co-ordination between various organizations dealing steel units etc. 
REPLY 
The Ministry of Steel has decided to formulate a National Steel Policy to have ;a national 
perspective and vision for the steel sector in the context of the second generation reforms, 
restructuring and globalisation. Ministry of Steel has already set up a drafting. Committee to draft 
a vision statement. The Committee is expected to submit its report within three months. The 
National Steel Policy will be finalised in consultation with major steel producers and consumers, 
their associations, suppliers of raw materials, financial institutions, Ministry of Coal, Commerce, 
Railways and Finance. 
FURTHER REPLY 
In pursuance of the directions of the Parliamentary Standing Committee On Industry, 
Ministry of Steel initiated action to formulate a National Steel Policy. A meeting was held under 
the chairmanship of Secretary (Steel) on 11.10.2000 which was attended by SAIL, TISCO, 
representatives of Planning Commission, Steel Furnace Association of India, CORSMA, CIT, All 
India Induction Furnace Association etc. A small drafting committee was set up to prepare the 
draft. The drafting committee is yet to submit the draft. The draft prepared by the drafting 
committee will be examined within the Ministry of Steel in consultation with Ministry of 
Finance, Commerce, Surface Transport, Railways and Coal. Thereafter, Ministry of Steel would 
go for wider consultation with all the major producers as well as Associations of steel producers 
and producers of raw materials for steel industry. In order to prepare the draft, DCI&S convened 
a meeting to discuss the blue prints of the draft policy and assign the work relating to various 
chapters to the experts in the fields. In an era of globalisation any national policy has to take into 
account not only the developments within the country but also developments in other countries & 
especially in view of the integration of the Indian steel industry with the global markets.

states having shortage of power. 
The Sub-Committee hopes that the Ministry of Steel will act in right earnest.

IMPLEMENTATION OF VOLUNTARY RETIREMENT SCHEME 
8 
RECOMMENDATION 
" The Sub-Committee is constrained to express its displeasure over the low productivity 
of labour in Indian Steel Industry which pushes the Industry to a disadvantageous point. In this 
regard, the respective plant management may be directed to resume that adequate training is 
imparted to the workers & various motivational scheme may be adopted to improve the labour 
productivity. 
The Committee, further, desires that the endeavour of rationalisation of manpower should 
continue with massive inputs on Scientific Human Resources management in order to achieve a 
'rational labour order' where high labour productivity may be obtained by employing efficient 
and effective labour force". 

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
In SAIL, labour productivity is calculated as "Production of Crude Steel including 
equivalent of Saleable Pig Iron assuming one tonne of Saleable Pig Iron equal to 0.25 tonnes of 
Crude' Steel divided by total number of Works Personnel in position excluding trainees of the 
plants". 
Labour productivity is usually expressed in terms of tonnes of Crude Steel produced per 
man year. The trend of Labour Productivity over the last few years has been as follows:-

The need for manpower rationalisation has been recognised within the company, and 
manpower has been reduced through natural separations, and operation of Voluntary Retirement 
Schemes in phases. 
A Financial and Business restructuring plan for SAIL has recently been approved by the 
Government of India and some of the non-core units will be divested. Right-sizing of manpower 
is one of the important areas of the plan. SAiL has prepared a plan to reduce its work force to 
• about one lakh by 2005 as against present strength of approximately 1.5 lakhs. 
The competency .and motivational levels of employees also contribute to the attainment 
of higher productivity levels .. SAIL has been impaqing training through its training institutes to 
enhance manpower utilisation. The system of unit training helps in defining standard operating 
practices to stream-line work flow and methods. Through multi-skilling, employees are 
encouraged to acquire additional allied skills to ensure complementarity and optimum utilisation 
between operations and maintenance functions. 
The incentive and reward schemes that are in vogue for all levels of executives and non­
executives have a component on producuon performance, in addition to cost and quality 
parameters. Capacity utilisatjon and fulfillnumt of Annual Performance Plan (APP) target on 
production are important parameters on which payments to employees are based. 
In the fiercely competitive steel market, enhancing productivity of work-force is an important tool 
for achieving higher profitability. Accordingly, all systems and schemes are being reviewed 
towards attainment of this goal. 

FURTHER REPLY 
(i) So far as SAIL is concerned the exercise to have rational labour is expected to be 
achieved in the next five years through Voluntary Retirement and other 
separations. This is as per MoU signed between SAIL and Government of India 
in terms of financial and business restructuring plan. 
(ii) Labour productivity depends on various factors like capacity of the plant, 
operating rate, employee's strength etc. Labour productivity varies widely not 
only between India and other Developed countries but also \\-ithin India between 
different steel producing units as measurement procedures and variables for 
calculation of labour productivity vary from unit to unit. 
So far as SAIL is concerned, the total ingot steel production in a year plus 25% of the pig 
iron production is divided by the manpower engaged in production process to arrive at the labour 
productivity. The labour productivity is around 95 tonnes/man year in SAIL.

problem of high cost of production due to one and other reasons which inter-alia include low 
labour productivity, high power tariff, obsolete tools and technology, high payment for 
procurement of raw material etc. which directly affects the pricing policy of the product and

undertake conscious efforts for reducing the cost of production. The Sub-committee is of the 
view that efforts may be made towards generat~on of high work culture, developmental 
supervision and progressive management, which backed by employment of latest technology for 
economisation of energy consumptions, would lead to reduction in the cost of production.

RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee is of the optmon that in a globalised and liberalized scenario 
formulation of marketing strategy has the telling impact on the profitability of corporate business . 
Henceforth, the Sub-Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry of Steel should 
formulate proper 'marketing policy' on the basis of which Central Marketing Organisation should 
chalk out effective marketing programmes which should be delivered to the marketing wing of 
the plant management and plant management should be given sufficient autonomy to act 
prudently keeping in mind the prevailing market scenario . Plant Management must strive at 
product promotion & product diversification & development in order to seize larger international 
market share. A proper market segmentation and brand endowment is the need of hour, besides 
stressing on consumer satisfaction . 
The Sub-Committee views that steel plants should adopt aggressive marketing strategy 
which will not only lead to disposal of inventories but also attainment of larger market share. 
REPLY 
With a view to evolve a Sales Plan attuned to the market conditions , a detailed exercise is 
undertaken before commencement of each financial year which, interalia, included the product­
wise, segment-wise demand vis-a-vis availability in the country as well as the production 
capabilities/constraints of each of the plant.

Group (MRG) Group of CMO of SAIL in consultation with the field marketing set up which is 
then deliberated extensively with the plant representatives for finalising the Sales Plan for the 
year.

booking are undertaken during the year as an on-going process and, in case any modification is 
warranted in the plan during the course of the year, depending on the prevailing market 
conditions, the same is carried out.

and efforts are made to execute the orders in terms of the customer's requirements. In order to 
compete in the highly competitive market, SAIL is reorienting its strategies/marketing initiatives 
based on the prevailing market conditions.

(i) To help increase market share and customer focus, CMO has undertaken 
organisational restructuring consisting of Flat Product Group and Long Product

and provide total service to major/strategic accounts in order to increase market 
share. 

(iii) Special emphasis on developing value added products through the efforts of R. &

(viii) Exploring ways to tap the potential Rural Demand.

20 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee feels that Usha Ispat Limited is a promising Pig Iron Plant and once 
the cloud of recession is off there would be a new morning for the Pig -Iron Industry. The Sub­
Committee is happy to note that UIL is the first Pig Iron Plant in India to get ISO certification. 
The Government 'should endeavor to encourage all such Pig Iron plant in private sector 
through tax & financial reforms which will not only lead to the prosperity of Steel industry but 
also lessen the dependence on import having its lasting impact on India's balance of payment. . \ 
REPLY 
'Iron and Steel'. including pig iron has been de-reserved and also de-licensed and the 
industry has been thrown open to the private sector for its development. In the post­
liberalisation era, the pig iron industry in India in the private sector has grown many fold. As a 
res.ult of various policy initiatives taken by the Government, the capacity of pig iron in the private 
sector has increased from merely one lakh tpa in l991-92lo over 3.53 million tpa in 1999-2000. 
The contribution of private/secondary sector units in the overall productions of pig iron in the 
country continued to increase. By 1999-2000, their contribution to the total production of 
approx. 3.2 million tonnes was about 60%. Today, India has emerged from a net importer of pig 
iron to a net exporter. 
FURTHER REPLY 
India's export of pig iron during 1997-98, 1998-99 and 1999-2000 were 0.79 million 
tonnes, 0.28 million tonnes and 0.29 million tonnes respectively. The above corresponds to 
about 5% of the global trade during 1997-1998 and around 2-2.5% during 98-99 and 99-2000. 

The Indian Pig Iron Industry, particularly those in the private sector are striving hard to 
reduce their costs of production and be competitive in the market. One of the deterrents is the 
higher cost of imported metallurgical coke which is mainly due to high rate of basic customs 
duty @ 15%. Ministry of Steel has been requesting repeatedly the M/o Finance to reduce the 
customs duty from 15% to 5% which has not been agreed to so far. Further, consumption of pig 
iron is directly dependent on the investment in the infrastructure. construction and engineering 
sectors. It is felt that general improvement of Indian economy and consequent higher domestic 
consumption of pig iron, resulting in higher sales realisation, will improve the performance of 
this sector.

GENERAL RECOMMENDATION 
Provision for sufficient fund-Row at sustainable rate of interest 
2 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee regards continuation of required fund flow as the life blood for steel 
industry which is capital intensive so development and growth of steel industry depends largely, 
on the degree of support from Government banks & other financial institution. Lack of sufficient 
working capitals funds for further modernization projects, high rate interest causing, increasing in 
cost of production due to debt burden & interest multiplication and hesitation on the part of 
Financial Institution in advancing further finance, to several units of steel industry etc. are the 
issues which require immediate reconsideration and evaluation. By the way, the Sub-Committee, 
considering the fact that steel industry, a sunrise industry, is passing through a cyclical recession, 
the financial institution should take a sympathetic view of steel industry & provide: -
(i) find for completion of on-going projects on priority basis; 
(ii) working capital facilities should also be made available at lower rates, because 
the Sub-Committee feels that primary producers find it difficult to extend the 
credit limit to their customers, so banks should be more forthcoming in extending 
working capital; 
(iii) Long term funding should be made available at the rate of 10 to 12% and the 
maternity of such debts may be 8 to 12 years; and 
(iv) As the steel plants has to spend about 15 to 20% of its project cost in developing 
infrastructure such as ports, roads, power distribution, fun"ds used for the 
development of such infrastructure projects may be considered at on interest rate 
of 10%. 
The Su~-Committee believes that the above support to steel industry from financial 
institutions will generate employment & enhance GOP growth. 
REPLY 
Government is aware of the issues which have been taken up in several forums and 
occasions. The issues were raised in the Round Table on Steel organised by the Ministry of Steel. 
As a follow-up of the Round Table, Ministry of Steel has constituted a Project Co-ordination 
Group (PCG) under the Chairmanship of the Steel Minister and Members consisting of 
Secretaries in the Ministries of Finance, Commerce, Power, CEOs of Financial Institutions 
(lOBI, IFCI & ICICI) ,State Bank of India .and President, Institute for Steel Development and 
Growth. The terms of reference of the PCG are as under:-

1. To find ways & means and suggest measures for early completion of the on-going iron and 
steel projects. 
2. To address the problems of existing I newly commissioned iron and steel plants with regard 
to the following : 
a. Demand generation; 
b. Customs and Excise Duty rationalization, 
c. Availability of power at reasonable prices, 
d. Measures to boost export , and 
e. Measures to restrict import of Steel . 
Subsequent to the constitution of the Project Co-ordination Group (PCG), two meetings 
of the Group were held on t 3.3.2000 and 1 I .9.2000 under the chainnanship of Minister of State 
for Steel. Various inputs were received on problems & issues related to the units. Specific issues 
like fund for completion of the on-going projects including their Working Capital requirements, 
lowering of interest rate etc. were also taken up for discussion during the meeting. The 
representatives of the Financial Institutions have generally agreed to provide need based support 
subject to observance of financial discipline by the promoters and also bringing in their equity as 
well as bringing back the diverted funds. The request on lowering of interest rate, however, did 
not find support by the Financial Institutions in view of the fact that this is a larger issue and 
concerns the economy as a whole. 
FURTHER REPLY 
(i) In the two meetings of the Project Co-ordination Group held so far, while no 
categorical assurance has been given to the new/upcoming steel units for 
supplying working capital, State Bank of India had shown its willingness to 
consider financing their share of working capital in respect of some units on 
merits subject to fulfillment of certain conditions. 
The Project Co-ordination Group was mainly constituted to find ways and means 
and suggest measures for early completion of the on-going projetts. As a 
facilitator,' the PCG has succeeded in creating an interface between the steel units 
and the financial institutions/commercial banks to address the problems of the 
industry. The PCG had discussed the problems relating to tenn loan as well as 
working capital requirements of different units with the financial institutions and 
SBI. The financial institutions/SBI have taken follow-up action on the decisions 
arrived at in the meetings ofthe PCG in respect of various units. 
(ii) The Union Budget for 2001-02 has reduced the interest rate on small savings by 
15 percentage points. RBI has also reduced the bank rate to 7%. This has 
resulted in reduction of PLR by most of the commercial banks and financial 
institutions by 0.25 to 0.5%. This reduction in PLR is accordingly, expected to 
reduce the interest rate in the procurement of working capital by the steel plants. 
Interest rates to steel plants vary from country to country and also unit to unit 
depending upon the PLR in the country and agreements with the lending bank. 
These in tum are governed by bank rate and many other factors including 
Government Policy, Reserve Bank Policy, rate of inflation etc. While there is no 
specific information on interest rates being availed by various steel producing 

units in the world, it is a fact that in most of the major steel producing countries, 
the interest rates are much lower than in India. 
(iii) Ministry of Steel at present has no proposal for setting up of Technology 
Development Upgradation Bank to meet the requirement of funds for 
modernisation of steel plants. The integrated steel plants viz. SAIL and TISCO 
are eligible to get concessional loan from Steel Development Fund. In so far as 
newly commissioned steel plants and plants in the pipe-line are concerned, it 
would be premature for them to consider any modernisation at this stage. The 
funds for modernisation of other plants, as and when required, can, be met by the 
existing financial institutions and commercial banks.

SPECIFIC RECOMMENDATION 
Ferro Scrap Nigam Limited {FSNL) 
2(i) 
RECOMMENDATION 
(i) Modernisation of Scrap Recovery Technology 
The Sub-Committee was made to understand that FSNL adopted Heckett's world class 
and world wide technology for carrying out the scrap recovery and processing operation. As the 
technology and equipments in FSNL became obsolete and old so it is pertinent that the plant 
should undergo modernisation process at the earliest in order to improve the physical and 
financial performance, henceforth FSNL management should work in the right earnest. 
REPLY 
There is no technology for scrap recovery other than magnetic separation. At FSNL 
magnetic separation is being carried out in mobile separation plants since inception. A feeding 
equipment i.e., Excavator is used for feeding this type of plant. However, FSNL is now setting up 
Modern Stationary Scrap Separation Plants at Durgapur & Vizag. These plants will have 
automatic vibrating grizzly feeder and will dispense with the feeding equipment. Crushing of 
slag and screening to various fractions will also be done after modernisation. 
FURTHER REPLY 
(i) Present status of Modern Stationary Scrap Separation Plant at DURGAPUR is given as 
under:-
All civil and structural drawings and detailed engineering have been completed. Tenders 
for civil construction and structural fabrication and erection jobs have been issued and work 
orders are expected to be released by end of March 200 I. 
All the equipment such as vibrating grizzly feeder, vibrating pan feeder, vibrating screen, 
belt conveyor components, rotary drum magnet, motors, control panels etc. are indigenously 
available and these have already been ordered and are expected to be received by August 200 I. 
Project cost of Plant is expected to be Rs.4.00 crores. 
VIZAG: 
Stationary plant is not proposed to be set up at present at Vizag Steel Plant because it has 
not been found to be economically viable due to very low scrap content in the L.D. Slag. 

Existing 3 Nos. mobile magnetic separators are adequate for fulfilliDJ the requirement of 
Visakhapetnam Steel Plant. 
TECHNOLOGY 
The technology involves automatic feeding of slag mixed with scrap by grizzly feeder 
into the feed hopper, separating metallics from slag by rotary magnetic drum separator and 
screening of the separated scrap into different sized fractions for reuse in Steel Melting Ship, 
Blast Furnace and Sintering Plant or for marketing. This is a proven technology established 
world over by M/s. Heckett Multiserv, who are the world leader in the area of scrap recovery and 
processing in steel plants. Same technology as used by M/s. Hec:kett Multiserv has been adopted 
and therefore there is no doubt about the usefulness of this proven technology in carrying out 
scrap recovery and processing to the full satisfaction of the Steel Plants.

Rationalisation of Freight 
10 
RECOMMENDATION 
During the course of interaction with workers and management the Sub-Committee came 
to know that freight charges are increased almost every year and as a result the steel industry has 
to face the consequences of high transportation cost. It is a matter to understand that steel industry 
being a heavy industry cost of transportation is itself high and if the freight is increased year after 
year it would be disastrous for steel industry. 
Moreover Sub-Committee has been apprised that in many a cases Railways charges the 
freight for the distance covered plus 30% which is illogical and unscientific. A case in this regard 
may be referred to the K.K. line ofVizag steel plant where RINL has to pay high charges to the 
Railway despite the fact that the cost of laying the rail platform has been realized much earlier. 
The Sub-Committee recommends that the Ministry of Steel should take up the issue of 
rationalization of freight charges in general and the case of K.K. route in particular, ~ith the 
Ministry of Railway at the earliest and resolve the issue without much delay. 
REPLY 
The Railway have been charging freight on Kimadul-Kottavalasa line (SE Railway) by 
inflating the distance by 30% NMDC has been representing for tbe removal of the same in view 
of the increased traffic handled on the line. 
The inflation in distance on K-K line had been continuing since 1967. Initially it was 
65.2%, but with the traffic volume increasing, this was reduced to ·30% in 1981.This percentage 
of inflation has been continuing since then. In the last eighteen years there has been significant 
increase in the traffic handled on K-K Line - originating iron ore movement has gone up from 
56.361akh tonnes in 1987-88 to 117lakh tonnes in 1997-98 and 124lakh tonnes in 1999-2000. In 
addition, the line has been handling other traffic particularly on account of the NALCO's alumina 
plant near Koraput. 
In addition to the budgetary increase in the freight charges over the years since 1981, 
Railways had been revising the classification of iron ore upwards resulting in further increasing in 
the freight charges. The classification of iron ore which was 110 in 1989-90 had increased to 120 
in 1994-95 and 125 in 1999-2000. For the FY 2000-2001, the Railway freight has been increased . 
by about 5% with downward revision in the classification from 125 to 120. The net result will be 
an increase of about 1% in the railway freight for the year 2000-2001 over the 1~99-2000 rate. 
The above two factors have greatly added to the freight burden on the pricing of iron ore 
from Bailadila Sector. 

The Ministry of Steel has taken up with Railways to withdraw the inflated mileage of 
30% on K-K line and freight charged on the basis of actual distance. However, Ministry of 
Railways informed that the concessional rates were granted by the S.E. Railway in 1999-2000 to 
increase the loading from KK line and the results of granting the concessiQn will be reviewed by 
Ministry of Railways at the end of 1999-2000 to appreciate the possible effect of reduction in 
distance inflation. 
Since NMDC have now poised to achieve the loading of iron ore from Bailadila Sector to 
be level of 13.2 M.T. during the current year, Ministry of Railways have again been requested to 
withdraw the 30% inflation in distance on KK line. 
Even, the Ministry of Steel had recommended to the Ministry of Railways to consider 
NMDC's proposal to take over the operations of K.K. line. But Ministry of Railways have not 
agreed to this proposal since the function of rail transportation has been assigned to Railways 
only and moreover NMDC has no expertise to operate any Railway system. The issue will be 
pursued with Ministry of Railways further. 
FURTHER REPLY 
The matter was again taken up with Ministry of Railway. In response, Ministry of 
Railways had intimated about their resource. crunch and advised this Ministry to make use of 
transport capacity available with railways for transportation of their raw material etc. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS 
The Committee feels that Steel being a heavy item even a slight increase in freight will 
definitely lead tQ higher transportation cost and in the ultimate analysis will affect the Steel 
Industry as a whole. That is why the Committee had recommended for rationalisation of 
freight charges. However, it is being felt that further that the Ministry of Steel will continue to 
persuade to the Ministry of Railway for rationalisation of freight charges or to provide 
concessional charges for transportation.of steel products. · 
The Committee notes· the service sector is becoming more and more competitive and 
many steel players have started steel transportation through roadways and if the trend gather 
the momentum there is a possibility that Railways may incur loss. Henceforth, it is in the 
mutual interest of the Railway and Steel lftdustry due consideration is paid by the Ministry of 
Railways towards rationalisation of freight charges, that so, also to attract potential consumer 
to continue Railway mode of transportation and not to let them switch over to Road ways. It is 
also in the. better interest of railway that large volume of heavy/bulky product is continued to be 
transported through railway instead of roadways. 
As far as the inflation in distance on kinnadua1-kotavasala'( K.K. Line) is concerned 
the Committee reiterates that the Ministry of Railways should reconsider the basic issue. Since 
the cost of laying the rail platfonn has been realised much earlier there remains hardly any 
rational ground to support the view of railways to continue for charging freight on K.K. Line 
by inflating the distance by 30% . A rational approach demands withdrawal of such inflated 
freight charges

REPLY OF 11IE GOVERNMENT

SALEM STEEL PLANT (SSP) 
15 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee discussed with workers, officers & management of SSP in detail the 
economic viability and rationale for demand for investment of further Rs. 600 crore for Steel 
melting Shop (SMS) vis-a-vis sluggish demand trend and loan and interest burden to be caused to 
SSP due to proposed installation of SMS and came to the conclusion that installation of -5MS is 
the need of hour. It is noteworthy that out of 48 stainless steel plant all over the world, SSP is the 
only unit without SMS facility. 
The Sub-Committee regards the SSP management's argument convincing which 
underlines the fact that installation of SMS banks on the principles of cost-benefit ratio because 
the existing cost on raw material is 66% of total cost and if SMS facilities are provided, the cost 
on raw material will come down to 45% or so, thus, providing leverage for cOmpetitiveness vis-a­
vis international market. Moreover, the installation of SMS facilities would provide favourable 
Break-Even-Point due to increment in volume of production and reduction in cost. 
Therefore, the Sub-Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry of Steel in 
general and SAD.. in particular should make conscious effort in this regard. 
~ REPLY 
As a step towards backward integration of Salem Steel Plant, steel-melting facilities were 
envisaged to be taken up during the -later part of 9tb Five-Year Plan. Due to fmancial constraints, 
it could not be considered so far. In view of scarcity of resources and high existing level of debts, 
SAIL is unable to provide desired level of funds to various units including that of Salem Steel 
Plant for installation of steel melting facilities, which are essential for technological upgradation 
and long-term viability. Salem Steel Plant is to be hived off inter alia as a part of finaQcial and 
business restructuring proposal. Possibility of forming a Joint Venture Company is being 
explored with two options viz. (i)-steel melting facilities may be set up by the Strategic Alliance 
Partner as a separate Joint Venture Company to supply input materials to SSP or (ii)- a Joint 
Venture Company for entire Salem Steel Plant and the Strategic Alliance Partner will set up steel 
melting facilities in a mutually agreed time schedule.

General Recommendation 
RATIONALISATION OF FREIGHT 
10 
The Committee feels that Steel being a heavy item even a slight increase in freight wilt 
definitely lead to higher transportation cost and in the ultimate analysis will affect the Steel 
Industry as a whole. That is why the Committee had rQCommended for rationalisation of 
freight charges. However, it is being felt that further that ihe Ministry of Steel will continue to 
persuade to the Ministry of Railway for rationalisation of freight charges or to provide 
concessional charges for transportation of steel products. 
The Committee notes the service sector is becoming more and more competitive and 
many steel player~ have started steel transpo11ation through roadways and if the trend gather 
the momentum there is a possibility that Railways may incur loss. Henceforth, it is in ~e 
mutual interest of the Railway and Steel Industry due consideration is paid by the Ministry of 
Railways towards rationalisation of freight charges, that so, also to attract potential consumer 
to continue Railway mode of transportation and not to let them switch over to Road ways . It is 
also in the better interest of railway that large volume of heavy/bulky product is continued to be 
transported through railway instead of roadways. 
As far as the inflation in distance on kirinadual-kotavasala ( K.K. Line) is COf\Cemed 
the Committee reiterates that the Ministry of Railways should reconsider the basic. Since the 
cost of laying the rail platform has been realised much earlier there remains hardly any rational 
ground to support the view of railways to continue for charging freight on K.K. Line by 
inflating the distance by 30% . A rational approach demands withdrawal of such inflated 
freight charges." 
MANAGEMENT BY OBJECI'IVES 
12 
The Cominittee·hopes that patchy years of SAIL will be over sooner then later if Steel PSUs 
management is honestly guided by the principle of management by objectives then 
management by activities. Memorandum of understanding is a unique tool to evaluate 
performance of a company. Target set, prioritization of parameters and objectives envisaged 
in MOU should act as the guiding force for actual realisation and implementation of 
programmes and course of action. Any deviation from the set target or objective or 
implementation gap makes the hole in the management network reflecting adverse credit in the 
MOU index. It is here that the vision and managerial skill has its role to play. Awarding of 
Fair credit to SAIL in the year 1997-98 and 1998-99 is testimony to the fact that individual 
· PSU management felt to tide over the turbulent water in steel industry, although recession in 
steel industry is a fact. Had the steel PSUs management , under SAIL applied its best, at least, 
SAIL as a whole would have not done so worse as it did actually. However, the Committee 

hopes that physical and financial perfonnance of SAIL as a whole will improve with the timely 
implementation business-cum-financial package for SAIL. 
The case of Alloy Steel Plant (ASP) is a pointer to the fact how the plant continues to 
languish in its physical and financial perfonnance due to the management found wanting in 
their role and responsibility. However, the Committee hopes that New Management of ASP 
will show its managerial skill in handling the situation. As Sub-Committee-! for Ministry of 
Steel visited ASP plant recently the matter will be dealt in a separate Report. 
Similarly, the Committee hopes that financial perfonnance of HSCL will improve under 
new management and with implementation of first phase of financial and business restructuring 
Programmes arid sanctioning of second phase of revival plan which is under the 
consideration of Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance.

existing level of inventories . The Committee reiterates the recommendation made earlier by

the inventories at each plant and will implement effectively the time bound strategic programme 
for disposal of inventories without further delay.

HINDUSTAN PAPER CORPORATION LTD – AN OVERVIEW
 
1.1       Hindustan Paper Corporation Ltd. (HPCL) incorporated in May 1970, is engaged in manufacture of paper,
paperboards, craft paper and newsprint. HPC is a Holding Company and has three Subsidiaries and two major integrated
pulp and paper Mills under its control.  These are:
 
Subsidiaries
 
Mandya National paper Mills Ltd.
Nagaland Pulp & Paper Company Ltd.
Hindustan Newsprint Ltd.
 
Units
 
Nagaon Paper Mills (NPM)
Cachar Paper Mills (CPM)
 
            The production of the Company (NPM and CPM) during the year 2000-2001 is likely to be Rs.424.14 crore.
 
Mandya National paper Mills Ltd.
 
1.2       Mandya National Paper Mills Ltd. (MNPM) was incorporated in the private sector in 1957.  After it became
sick, HPC took over the management of this mill in January 1974 as a result of the tripartite agreement between
Government of Karnataka, HPC and MNPM.  HPC holds 97.8% of equity share capital and entire preference shares. 
The company became sick and was referred to BIFR.  Karnataka High Court have since pronounced winding up of the
company on 20.10.2000.
 
Nagaland Pulp & Paper Company Ltd.
 
1.3       Nagaland Pulp and Paper Company Ltd. (NPPC) is a subsidiary of Hindustan Paper Corporation (HPC).  HPC
hold 95% of the equity shares and the Government of Nagaland hold 5%.  The company which came out of the purview
of BIFR due to financial restructuring again became sick as the revival scheme could not be put into operation due to
law and order problem, lack of infrastructure and absence of banking facilities.  Government has communicated its
stand to BIFR that it will accept any decision of BIFR including winding up.  In the meanwhile, on NPPC’s request
BIFR has asked the company to prepare a revival plan and direct OA to submit a report.  There is no production activity
in the plant.

2.1       During the course of the meeting the workers union expressed certain problem at the technical level, which
affected the morale and motivation of the workers like overdue wage revision etc. DHI confirmed that this has been
addressed to.  Besides, both the workers’ union and the management emphasised the need for extending excise duty
holiday to these mills located in the NE as is extended to other units set up in the NE after 1997.  Besides, the workers
union and the management also proposed that government departments should buy their paper requirements from the
HPC.  Moreover, both emphasised before the sub-committee that their proposal for captive plantation should be
expedited to enable continuous operation of these plants.  In addition, the management also highlighted the need for
extending transport subsidy to the HPC units located in the NE region.
 
2.2       Department of Heavy Industries had earlier issued a pay revision notice besides having taken up the issues of
transport subsidy, excise duty exemption to the NE located units and also expediting of captive plantation with the
respective ministries, as conveyed vide its ATR of 16th August 2000.  However, the persuasive efforts of Department of
Heavy Industries were not bearing much fruit.  Besides it was observed by the sub-committee that these issues needed to
be approached through a coordinated effort and moreover the sub-committee also felt that there was a lack of
appreciation of concerns expressed by the Department of Heavy Industry in respect of HPC’s operation by the other
ministries.  The sub-committee felt that at the strategic level the problems facing industrial units in the NE,
notwithstanding whether it was private or public sector, were uniform and similar.
 
2.3       Issues like aforestation for captive purposes, transport subsidy, excise duty exemption, etc. encompassed all
these units.  Hence, the sub-committee sought to hear the views of public sector as well as the private sector located in
the NE.  It heard the view of the industries in the NE both in the public and the private sector on 8
th  August 2001.  It
emanated from the views expressed by these that not only were the problems of the units grave but it was being further
aggravated by a Supreme Court order of 13thDecember 1996 related to debarring private plantation in the NE which
violated the constitutional guaranteed rights of the local tribals of the NE under article 371A-D and 371-H of the
Constitution.  It came to the observation of the sub-committee that this situation was leading to an insurgency in the NE
region and needed to be addressed on priority. The Convenor, Sub-Committee-III thereafter called upon the Secretaries
of Ministries of Environment and Forest, Law, Industrial Policy and Promotion, Banking and Revenue, Heavy Industry,
Railways and HPC on 21
st August, 2001  to begin process of dialogue through which some of the issues could be
resolved. The sub-committee noted that discussions with the Member Traffic, Railway Board, had resolved the
problems of HPCL.  Other Secretaries present in this meeting decided to deliberate in detail and come back to the sub-
committee within a period of four weeks.
 
2.4       On September 27, 2001, the Secretaries came back to the sub-committee.  In the meantime, the government had
also formed a new Department  of the Development of  North-East and the Hon’ble Minister of North-Eastern
Development had also expressed his eagerness to be educated on the sub-committee’s findings and their interaction in
the matter so far.  Hence, he was also requested to join the meeting as a special invitee.  In this meeting, the Hon’ble
Minister began with the opening remarks that it would not be appropriate to expect government investments to
rejuvenate   the North East.  The need and focus of the government was to think of ways by which local initiative

Industrial Scenario in the North Eastern Region and Sub-Committee’s Findings,
Observations and Recommendations
 
3.1       The entire North East region is very sensitive and has been witnessing troubled socio-political disturbances since
long.  As a consequence, the economic development has suffered badly, resulting in poor industrial growth.
 
3.2       The main reason for insurgency in the North East was the alienation of the people, which began immediately
after independence. The government has taken some initiatives and a sizable number of insurgents have laid down
arms.  But immediately after, they have starting looking for employment.  Internal security problems cannot be resolved
if such issues cannot be addressed.
 
3.3       Every government that has come to power at the centre has been concerned about the development in the North
East but progress has been rather tardy, if not stagnant, despite announcement of special economic packages.  In 1995,
North East Development Bank with an authorised capital of Rs.500 crores was created but how far it has helped
expansion and modernisation of industrial enterprises is not known.  The region still lacks good roads, water and
electricity, the basic needs for development.  What can help boost growth is collection of unspent balance of the
amounts earmarked for different Union Ministries and spending of the same in the region with the emphasis on the
feasible projects and sustaining the existing industries, which are facing difficulties.  It has two objectives – one is the
survival of the industry and the second is the generation of employment.  The main objective is, however, the reduction
of insurgency.  The existing units should be helped so that they can meet the social obligation, develop the area,
generate employment.  Everything should not be seen from the revenue point of view.  Unless existing industries
survive, no investment from outside North East is likely to come as is evident from the fact that after 1997 no new
projects have come to the region.  The fiscal concessions along with peace initiative will change the economic climate
of North East and bring it in the mainstream of country and it will not be viewed as a distant territory.
3.4       The Government of India had granted certain incentives to some specified industries located in the North East. 
Their incentives were mainly in the form of excise duty relief and capital investment subsidy.  The incentives are
applicable only for those who started production after 24
th December 1997.  The transport subsidy scheme 1971 was
also included in the above policy.  This step is in fact to encourage the industrial growth in the North East region.  The
underlying idea behind extending these incentives was to provide the much needed impetus to the North Eastern states
so that the region could overcome its backwardness and the difficulties faced by it on account of geographical isolation
and provide them a level playing field.  The ultimate goal was to facilitate setting up of new industries and sustain those,
which exist thus paving the way for all round economic development of the region.  However, due to the incorporation
of the cut-off date of 24
th December 1997, a large section of the industries in the area prior to this date were left
uncovered by those well-intended notifications.
 
3.5       The industrial activity in the North Eastern states can be attributed to four industries- (a)  forest-base   industries
like pulpwood using paper industries and wood-using plywood and veneer industry (b)  tea plantation (c) refineries (d) 
ancillary and allied  activities based on requirement for   the aforesaid three  industries.
 
Findings of  the Sub-Committee relating to  Pulp  Wood  Paper  Industry
 
4.1       HPC's two mills located in the north eastern sector, having all potentialities to operate at the  rated  capacity,
have been carrying huge liability payable to Government of India, which had accrued during initial  periods of 
operations, when the production did not stablise.  Although  the  production could  be stablised from 1994-95, after
implementation of  de-bottlenecking scheme , the production did not stabilise.  Although the production could be
stabilised from 1994-95, after implementation of de-bottlenecking schemes, the production could not be maximised due
to depressed market conditions.  Now, although the paper market has shown some signs of improvement, it is felt that
because of the cyclical nature of Indian paper industry, the boom period may not last for a long time.  Moreover, the
Indian paper markets, including newsprint market, are closely linked with international paper market scenario, which is

             HPC solicits the following reliefs:
 
Restoration of transport subsidy and waiving  of excise duty for Cachar Paper Mills.
Allotment of degraded forest land for raising the captive plantation in Assam.
Timely  allotment of wagons and expeditious conversion of meter gauge railway line to broad gauge in Lumding-
Silchar sector to avoid transhipment.
 
Continuing of Transport Subsidy and Waiving  of Excise Duty
to Cachar Paper Mills
 
4.2       Cachar Paper Mill (CPM) located in the southern part of Assam, experiences more locational disadvantages than
Nagaon Paper Mill and the freight charges incurred by the mill, both for transporting inputs and products, are very high
as compared to other mills.  The paper produced by Cachar Paper Mill is mostly sold in the Northern region.  Due to
higher element of freight, the mill fails to procure institutional orders from Northern region in competition with other
paper manufacturers.
 
4.3       The transport subsidy was introduced by the Government of India to lessen the burden of heavy transportation
cost incurred by the industries located in the North-Eastern sector for movement of raw materials and finished products
from certain selected rail heads.  So far as the locational disadvantages for Cachar Paper Mills are concerned, there is no
improvement in the situation from what prevailed at the time of commissioning of the mill.  Moreover, the freight
charges are increasing day by day, causing more financial outgo from the mill.  The rail head at CPM being a meter
gauge, all the incoming materials and outgoing finished products are transhipped at Lumding which results in avoidable
delay and wastage due to transhipment.  The problem becomes worst during rainy season  additionally due to landslides.
 
4.4       Under the new industrial policy for the North Eastern region, finalised by the Government in December 1997,
the units located in the North Eastern sector are eligible for transport subsidy only for the first five years of commercial
production till 31.3.2007.  in addition, all the units in these zones would be free from income tax, excise, for a  period of
10 years from the commencement of production.
 
4.5       The rationale for transport subsidy is to mitigate the high cost of transportation of raw material and finished
product due to location of the units in remote, hilly inaccessible areas of the country, where the infrastructure is poor.
 
4.6       The transportation cost at NPM and CPM for raw materials and finished products from and to the main lands is
extremely high and hence needs to be mitigated through extension of the subsidy.  The grant of transport subsidy should
be viewed in a different light.  While the units through improved performance may become economically viable even
after tax holiday, the transportation cost does not get mitigated unless the requisite infrastructure is developed.
 
4.7       The southern part of Assam, where the CPM is situated, is highly monsoon prone area and the roads are
inundated with flood waters every year and land slides occur causing disruption of roads movement for about 2-3
months in a year.  Thus, CPM deserves some fiscal concessions from the Government to become a viable unit.
 
4.8       In view of the above, HPC appealed to the Government of India to include the existing establishments which are
continuously being affected adversely due to their locational disadvantages, like the CPM, under the new industrial
policy and grant exemption of excise duty payment for a period of 10 years and to revive the transport subsidy scheme
effective from April 1995 as a special case for CPM.
 
Allotment of Degraded Forest Land for the Development Of Captive Plantation
 
4.9       In order to become self-sufficient in meeting with requirement of bamboo for the two mills of HPC and to
reverse the deficiency of forest resources in general, the need for taking up the captive plantation by HPC should be
recognized and clearance be given.  This also has a beneficial effect to social upliftment due to the manpower required
for this activity.  Since early 1990, HPC has been appealing to the Government of Assam, Ministry of Environment and
